title: Japan 20-Year JGB auction (¥700bn anticipated, issue 198 expected new) — the tenor the BoJ tapered hardest, and the auction-level test of the bucket mechanism
source: EST: mof.go.jp English October 2026 auction calendar (policy/jgbs/auction/calendar/2610e.htm), re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 24,853 bytes — byte-identical to the jgb-30y-auction-2026-10-08 lane's 2026-09-08 fetch, so nothing on the page has moved); its table row reads 'Oct. 20, 2026 | 20-year'. The DATE is MOF's own. The SIZE is anticipated, not announced: no October row carries an announcement href on 2026-09-09, and MOF's own note on the page reads 'Each issue amount will be announced about one week prior to each auction date', putting terms around 2026-10-13. The ¥700bn anticipated size comes from a second MOF primary, the Auction Results for JGBs workbook (english/policy/jgbs/auction/past_auction_results/Auction_Results_for_JGBs.xls, 492,032 bytes, last saved 2026-08-13, downloaded and parsed 2026-09-09): the 20-year runs monthly and MOF cut it from ¥1,000bn to ¥800bn on 2025-07-10 and to ¥700bn from 2026-04-14, where it has stayed for every auction since. Confirmed at the most recent print from a third MOF primary the workbook does not yet carry — result page eresul/eresul20260820.htm (HTTP 200, fetched direct 2026-09-09) — whose ¥532.1bn competitive plus ¥167.4bn non-price-competitive I sums to ¥699.5bn against a ¥700bn offering. Filed `estimate` on the same two counts every JGB entry on this calendar records: the size is anticipated rather than announced, and market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a non-US sovereign debt office. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Proposed 2026-09-08 by the jgb-30y-auction-2026-10-08 initial-research adjacency sweep (proposals/jgb-20y-auction-2026-10-20.from-jgb-30y-auction-2026-10-08.json, read as input and now shadowed by this canonical file); researched 2026-09-09 (docs/research/events/jgb-20y-auction-2026-10-20.md). THE JOB THE 30-YEAR LEDGER ASSIGNED THIS EVENT WAS TO FALSIFY ITS OWN MECHANISM, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THE MECHANISM DOES NOT REACH AUCTION DEMAND. That ledger predicted the 20-year is 'the tenor where auction demand should deteriorate first' because the BoJ tapered the 10-25y bucket -55% while leaving 25y+ flat. Tested as a difference-in-differences with the 30-year as control, month-matched, across the exact window where the two buckets diverged (2024-01 -> 2025-03, both flat, vs 2025-04 -> 2026-09, 10-25y falling ¥450bn -> ¥200bn): the 20-year's tail did NOT widen relative to the 30-year's — it narrowed, +0.45bp -> +0.04bp, DiD -0.41bp at t = -0.77, with the cover gap +0.05 at t = +0.29; continuous, corr(BoJ 10-25y purchases, 20Y-minus-30Y tail gap) = +0.073 (t = +0.47, n=44 month-matched pairs). What DID deteriorate is the tenor the mechanism says kept its buyer: the 30-year's mean tail rose 0.90 -> 1.64bp (t = +2.66) while the 20-year's moved 1.35 -> 1.66bp (t = +0.55). Power is honest at ~1.5bp. TWO PRIMARY-SOURCED FINDINGS EXPLAIN WHY THE TENOR-LABEL MAPPING WAS TOO CLEAN. (1) The bucket is not a tenor. Summing every outstanding coupon issue in MOF's own workbook by remaining maturity at 2026-10-20, the tapered 'more than 10 and up to 25 years' bucket holds ¥244.8trn, of which only 52.2% is 20-year paper — 45.8% is SEASONED 30-year paper. Read the other way, ¥112.1trn of the ¥171.0trn of 30-year paper outstanding — 66% — sits in the TAPERED bucket against 28% (¥48.8trn) in the untapered one. Normalised on that float instead of on new supply, the BoJ absorbed 0.184%/month of the 10-25y bucket and 0.165% of 25y+ in 2024-01 (1.12x) against 0.082% and 0.165% in 2026-08 (0.50x) — a real asymmetry, roughly a factor of two, not the -55%-versus-zero the tenor labels imply. (2) The sibling's window starts where the 25y+ taper stopped. Re-reading the BoJ operation files back to 2023-01 (44 monthly workbooks, boj.or.jp/en/statistics/boj/fm/ope/m_release) reproduces its 2024-01 -> 2026-08 table exactly and then shows 25y+ ALSO tapered, ¥301.6bn (2023-06) -> ¥150.4bn (2026-08), -50%, against 10-25y's -75% over the same span; both buckets roughly halved in the 2023-12 -> 2024-01 step. This is the same window-start artifact that ledger corrected in ITS siblings. WHERE THE BUCKET BOUNDARY IS VISIBLE IS THE CURVE, AND AT 25 YEARS RATHER THAN 30. On MOF's par curve at 2026-09-08 the 25-year yield (3.974%) is ABOVE the 30-year (3.961%): 20s25s stands at +25.7bp, the 94.1st percentile of 5,501 sessions (median +13.7), while 25s30s is -1.3bp, the 1.0th percentile (median +8.5). The 25Y has printed above the 30Y in 63 sessions since 2026-05-27, out of 83 in the entire history. The kink sits on the BoJ's own boundary, not on the 30-year; 20s30s reads only the 66.3rd percentile because it spans the boundary and averages the two halves. Offered as association plus mechanism — MOF's 25-year par point is fitted, not a traded on-the-run issue, and a spline artifact is not ruled out. THE SPILLOVER NULL IS UPGRADED, NOT REPEATED: the 09-15 sibling's n=44 test extends to 275 auctions (2003-10-21 -> 2026-08-20) matched to the same-date US 20Y CMT, and this tenor never even looks significant raw (soft tail >=2bp, n=20, precedes +1.55bp vs -0.21bp firm, diff +1.76bp, t = +1.24) before the 30-year ledger's control kills it (corr(tail, same-date JGB 20Y move) +0.417 at t = +7.57; partial corr(tail, US | JGB) +0.027 at t = +0.45; D+1 +0.042, t = +0.69). The sibling's 2023+ figures reproduce exactly (t = +0.80), which is the check that the pipelines agree. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is `low`: no tracked symbol carries yen-rates exposure, no house playbook is rates-keyed, and the one channel that could have justified an entry is the refuted one. Unlike 2026-09-15, the US 20-year is D+1 (treasury-20y-bond-2026-10-21), not same-day, which makes this the cleaner sequencing instrument of the two. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
